title.raw: 《田單列傳》 Biography of Tian Dan

sentences.zh: 田單者，齊諸田疏屬也。

translations.literal: Tian Dan was Qi various Tian distant relative.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan was a distant relation of the Tian clan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 湣王時，單為臨菑市掾，不見知。

translations.literal: Min Wang time, Dan was Linzi market assistant, not seen known.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of King Min, Dan served as a minor official in the marketplace of Linzi, unknown to anyone of importance.

sentences.zh: 及燕使樂毅伐破齊，齊湣王出奔，已而保莒城。

translations.literal: When Yan sent Yue Yi attacked broke Qi, Qi Min Wang fled out, soon after defended Ju city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan sent Yue Yi to attack and defeat Qi, King Min of Qi fled the capital and eventually took refuge in the city of Ju.

sentences.zh: 燕師長驅平齊，而田單走安平，令其宗人盡斷其車軸末而傅鐵籠。

translations.literal: Yan army long drove pacified Qi, yet Tian Dan fled Anping, ordered his clansmen all cut their cart axle ends and attached iron cages.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yan army swept through and conquered Qi, Tian Dan fled to Anping, where he ordered all his clansmen to saw off the protruding ends of their cart axles and cap them with iron sheaths.

sentences.zh: 已而燕軍攻安平，城壞，齊人走，爭涂，以折車敗，為燕所虜，唯田單宗人以鐵籠故得脫，東保即墨。

translations.literal: Soon after Yan army attacked Anping, city broken, Qi people fled, contended roads, with broken carts defeated, captured by Yan, only Tian Dan clansmen because iron cage reason got escape, east defended Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Yan army attacked Anping. When the walls were breached, the people of Qi fled, jostling for space on the roads. Their cart axles snapped, their vehicles broke down, and they were captured by the Yan forces. Only the Tian clan, thanks to their iron-sheathed axles, managed to escape and fled east to hold the city of Jimo.

sentences.zh: 燕既盡降齊城，唯獨莒、即墨不下。

translations.literal: Yan having all surrendered Qi cities, only alone Ju, Jimo not fell.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan had taken the surrender of every city in Qi, only Ju and Jimo remained unconquered.

sentences.zh: 燕軍聞齊王在莒，并兵攻之。

translations.literal: Yan army heard Qi king in Ju, combined troops attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army learned that the King of Qi was in Ju, they concentrated their forces to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 淖齒既殺湣王於莒，因堅守，距燕軍，數年不下。

translations.literal: After Nao Chi had killed King Min in Ju, they thereupon held firm, resisted the Yan army, and for several years the city did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: After Nao Chi had killed King Min in Ju, the city nonetheless held firm and resisted the Yan army; for several years it did not fall.

sentences.zh: 燕引兵東圍即墨，即墨大夫出與戰，敗死。

translations.literal: Yan led troops east surrounded Jimo, Jimo grandee went out fought with them, defeated died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then led its troops east to besiege Jimo. The magistrate of Jimo marched out to give battle but was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 城中相與推田單，曰：「安平之戰，田單宗人以鐵籠得全，習兵。」

translations.literal: City middle mutually pushed Tian Dan, said: 'Anping battle, Tian Dan clansmen with iron cages got whole, familiar with troops.'
translations.idiomatic: The people within the city conferred and put forward Tian Dan, saying, "During the battle at Anping, the Tian clan survived intact thanks to their iron-sheathed axles. He understands the art of war."

sentences.zh: 立以為將軍，以即墨距燕。

translations.literal: Established him as general, with Jimo resisted Yan.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed him general, and he used Jimo as his stronghold to resist Yan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，燕昭王卒，惠王立，與樂毅有隙。

translations.literal: Soon after, Yan Zhao Wang died, Hui Wang ascended, with Yue Yi had rift.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, King Zhao of Yan died and King Hui succeeded him. The new king bore a grudge against Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 田單聞之，乃縱反閒於燕，宣言曰：「齊王已死，城之不拔者二耳。

translations.literal: Tian Dan heard this, then released reverse spies in Yan, declared said: 'Qi king already dead, cities not captured two only.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Dan learned of this, he sent double agents into Yan to spread a rumor: "The King of Qi is already dead, and only two cities remain uncaptured.

sentences.zh: 樂毅畏誅而不敢歸，以伐齊為名，實欲連兵南面而王齊。

translations.literal: Yue Yi feared execution and dared not return; taking the attack on Qi as a pretext, he truly wished to hold his army together, face south, and make himself king of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi feared execution and dared not return home. He used the campaign against Qi as a pretext, but his true ambition was to keep command of his army, face south, and make himself king of Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊人未附，故且緩攻即墨以待其事。

translations.literal: The people of Qi had not yet submitted, so he deliberately delayed the attack on Jimo to wait for his plans.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi had not yet submitted to him, so he deliberately delayed the attack on Jimo while he waited for his plans to ripen.

sentences.zh: 齊人所懼，唯恐他將之來，即墨殘矣。」

translations.literal: Qi people what fear, only fear other general come, Jimo finished.'
translations.idiomatic: What the people of Qi truly fear is that another general might come to replace him — then Jimo would be finished."

sentences.zh: 燕王以為然，使騎劫代樂毅。

translations.literal: Yan king considered it so, sent Qi Jie replace Yue Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Yan believed the rumor and sent Qi Jie to replace Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 樂毅因歸趙，燕人士卒忿。

translations.literal: Yue Yi thus returned Zhao, Yan officials soldiers angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi thereupon fled to Zhao, and the Yan officers and soldiers were filled with resentment.

sentences.zh: 而田單乃令城中人食必祭其先祖於庭，飛鳥悉翔舞城中下食。

translations.literal: Yet Tian Dan then ordered city middle people eat must sacrifice their ancestors in courtyard, flying birds all soar dance city middle eat food.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan then ordered every household in the city to set out offerings to their ancestors in the courtyard before each meal. Flocks of birds swooped and circled above the city to feed on the offerings.

sentences.zh: 燕人怪之。

translations.literal: Yan people strange it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 田單因宣言曰：「神來下教我。」

translations.literal: Tian Dan thus declared said: 'Spirit come down teach me.'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan seized the moment and proclaimed, "A spirit has descended to instruct me."

sentences.zh: 乃令城中人曰：「當有神人為我師。」

translations.literal: Then ordered city middle people said: 'Should have divine person be my teacher.'
translations.idiomatic: He told the people of the city, "A divine being shall serve as my teacher."

sentences.zh: 有一卒曰：「臣可以為師乎？」

translations.literal: One soldier said: 'Your servant could serve as teacher?'
translations.idiomatic: One of the soldiers said, "Might I serve as your teacher?"

sentences.zh: 因反走。

translations.literal: Thus, turned fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then he turned and ran away.

sentences.zh: 田單乃起，引還，東鄉坐，師事之。

translations.literal: Tian Dan then rose, drew back, east facing sat, teacher served him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan rose, led the man back, seated him in the place of honor facing east, and treated him with the deference owed to a master.

sentences.zh: 卒曰：「臣欺君，誠無能也。」

translations.literal: Soldier said: 'Minister deceived lord, truly without ability.'
translations.idiomatic: The soldier protested, "I have deceived you, my lord. I truly have no abilities."

sentences.zh: 田單曰：「子勿言也！」

translations.literal: Tian Dan said: 'Child not speak!'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan replied, "Say nothing more of it!"

sentences.zh: 因師之。

translations.literal: Thus, teacher him.
translations.idiomatic: And so he treated the man as his divine teacher.

sentences.zh: 每出約束，必稱神師。

translations.literal: Every go out regulations, must call divine teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he issued orders, he invariably invoked the authority of the divine teacher.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言曰：「吾唯懼燕軍之劓所得齊卒，置之前行，與我戰，即墨敗矣。」

translations.literal: Then he declared, saying: 'I only fear that the Yan army will cut off the noses of the Qi soldiers they have captured and place them in the front ranks to fight us — then Jimo will be lost.'
translations.idiomatic: Then he spread a rumor, saying, "My only fear is that the Yan army will cut off the noses of the Qi prisoners they have captured and place them in the front ranks to fight against us — then Jimo will surely fall."

sentences.zh: 燕人聞之，如其言。

translations.literal: Yan people heard this, as his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops heard the rumor and did exactly as he had suggested.

sentences.zh: 城中人見齊諸降者盡劓，皆怒，堅守，唯恐見得。

translations.literal: City middle people saw Qi various surrendered ones all noses cut, all angry, firm defend, only fear be captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the people in the city saw that every Qi prisoner who had surrendered had been mutilated by having his nose cut off, they were consumed with fury. They defended the walls with renewed determination, dreading above all else the prospect of being captured.

sentences.zh: 單又縱反閒曰：「吾懼燕人掘吾城外冢墓，僇先人，可為寒心。」

translations.literal: Dan again released reverse spies said: 'I fear Yan people dig my city outside tombs graves, mutilate ancestors, can be chilling heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan again sent double agents to spread a rumor: "What I dread most is that the Yan troops will dig up the tombs outside our city walls and desecrate our ancestors. The very thought chills my heart."

sentences.zh: 燕軍盡掘壟墓，燒死人。

translations.literal: Yan army all dug up mounds graves, burned dead people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army dug up every grave mound and tomb and burned the corpses.

sentences.zh: 即墨人從城上望見，皆涕泣，俱欲出戰，怒自十倍。

translations.literal: Jimo people from city wall saw, all tears wept, all wished go out battle, anger from ten times.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jimo watched from atop the city walls, and every one of them wept. All burned to march out and fight, their fury multiplied tenfold.

sentences.zh: 田單知士卒之可用，乃身操版插，與士卒分功，妻妾編於行伍之閒，盡散飲食饗士。

translations.literal: Tian Dan knew the troops could be used, then personally took up mattock and spade, shared labor with the soldiers, had wives and concubines weave among the ranks, and gave out all food and drink to feast the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan knew his soldiers were ready. He took up mattock and spade and labored alongside them, sharing in their toil. He placed his own wives and concubines among the ranks and distributed all his food and drink to feast the troops.

sentences.zh: 令甲卒皆伏，使老弱女子乘城，遣使約降於燕，燕軍皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Ordered armored soldiers all hide, made old weak women defend city, sent envoy agree surrender to Yan, Yan army all called ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the armored soldiers to conceal themselves and had the old, the weak, and the women man the walls. Then he sent an envoy to negotiate terms of surrender with Yan. The Yan army all cheered in triumph.

sentences.zh: 田單又收民金，得千溢，令即墨富豪遺燕將，曰：「即墨即降，願無虜掠吾族家妻妾，令安堵。」

translations.literal: Tian Dan again collected people's gold, got thousand yi, ordered Jimo rich merchants send to Yan general, said: 'Jimo immediately surrender, wish not plunder our clan families wives concubines, let peaceful dwell.'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan also collected gold from the people, amassing a thousand yi, and had the wealthy merchants of Jimo deliver it to the Yan general with the message: "Jimo is about to surrender. We beg only that you not plunder the families, wives, and concubines of our clans, but let them dwell in peace."

sentences.zh: 燕將大喜，許之。

translations.literal: Yan general greatly happy, promised it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general was overjoyed and agreed to their terms.

sentences.zh: 燕軍由此益懈。

translations.literal: Yan army from this increasingly lax.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, the Yan army grew ever more complacent.

sentences.zh: 田單乃收城中得千餘牛，為絳繒衣，畫以五彩龍文，束兵刃於其角，而灌脂束葦於尾，燒其端。

translations.literal: Tian Dan then collected city middle got thousand plus oxen, made crimson silk clothes, painted with five colors dragon patterns, bound weapons on their horns, and poured oil bundled reeds on tails, burned their ends.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan then gathered more than a thousand oxen from within the city. He had them draped in coverings of crimson silk painted with brilliant dragon patterns in five colors, and blades were lashed to their horns. Bundles of oil-soaked reeds were tied to their tails and set alight.

sentences.zh: 鑿城數十穴，夜縱牛，壯士五千人隨其後。

translations.literal: Drilled city several tens holes, night released oxen, strong warriors five thousand followed their rear.
translations.idiomatic: He had dozens of openings cut through the city walls. Under cover of night, the oxen were released, and five thousand picked warriors followed behind them.

sentences.zh: 牛尾熱，怒而奔燕軍，燕軍夜大驚。

translations.literal: Oxen tails hot, angry charged Yan army, Yan army night greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: The heat at their tails maddened the oxen, and they charged straight into the Yan camp. The Yan army was thrown into panic in the darkness.

sentences.zh: 牛尾炬火光明炫燿，燕軍視之皆龍文，所觸盡死傷。

translations.literal: The oxen's tail torches blazed bright and dazzling; the Yan army looked and saw only dragon patterns, and whatever was struck was killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The torches at the oxen's tails blazed with dazzling light, and in the glare the Yan troops saw only dragon patterns. Whatever the oxen struck was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 五千人因銜枚擊之，而城中鼓譟從之，老弱皆擊銅器為聲，聲動天地。

translations.literal: Five thousand thus bit wooden gag attacked them, and city middle drums roared followed, old weak all struck bronze vessels for sound, sound moved heaven earth.
translations.idiomatic: The five thousand warriors, with wooden gags clenched between their teeth to ensure silence, fell upon the enemy. From within the city, drums thundered and the old and weak beat on bronze vessels, raising a clamor that shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 燕軍大駭，敗走。

translations.literal: Yan army greatly terrified, defeated fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was utterly terrified and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 齊人遂夷殺其將騎劫。

translations.literal: Qi people then annihilated killed their general Qi Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Qi pursued and slew the Yan general Qi Jie.

sentences.zh: 燕軍擾亂奔走，齊人追亡逐北，所過城邑皆畔燕而歸田單，兵日益多，乘勝，燕日敗亡，卒至河上，而齊七十餘城皆復為齊。

translations.literal: Yan army confused fled, Qi people pursued defeated chased fleeing, what passed cities all rebelled Yan returned to Tian Dan, troops daily increased, riding victory, Yan daily defeated perished, finally reached Yellow River, yet Qi seventy plus cities all recovered as Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army scattered in chaos and flight. The men of Qi gave chase, pursuing the vanquished and routing the fugitives. Every city and town they passed through revolted against Yan and rallied to Tian Dan. His forces grew by the day. Pressing their advantage, they drove the Yan forces back until at last they reached the banks of the Yellow River, and all seventy-odd cities of Qi were restored to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 乃迎襄王於莒，入臨菑而聽政。

translations.literal: Then welcomed Xiang Wang from Ju, entered Linzi listened to government.
translations.idiomatic: They then welcomed King Xiang from Ju, and he entered Linzi to take up the governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 襄王封田單，號曰安平君。

translations.literal: Xiang Wang enfeoffed Tian Dan, titled An Ping Jun.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang enfeoffed Tian Dan and bestowed upon him the title Lord of Anping.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：兵以正合，以奇勝。

translations.literal: Grand Historian said: Warfare with orthodox engages, with extraordinary wins.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: In warfare, one engages with the orthodox and achieves victory through the extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 善之者，出奇無窮。

translations.literal: Skilled at it ones, produce extraordinary inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: Those who master this art produce the extraordinary in inexhaustible measure.

sentences.zh: 奇正還相生，如環之無端。

translations.literal: Extraordinary orthodox mutually give birth, like ring without end.
translations.idiomatic: The extraordinary and the orthodox give rise to each other in turn, like a ring without beginning or end.

sentences.zh: 夫始如處女，適人開戶；

translations.literal: Indeed beginning like virgin, enemy opens door;
translations.idiomatic: At first one is as still as a maiden, so that the enemy opens his door;

sentences.zh: 後如脫兔，適不及距：其由單之謂邪！

translations.literal: Later like escaped rabbit, enemy cannot block: this from Dan called!
translations.idiomatic: then one strikes like a hare set free, too swift for the enemy to resist — is this not precisely what is meant by Tian Dan!

sentences.zh: 初，淖齒之殺湣王也，莒人求湣王子法章，得之太史嬓之家，為人灌園。

translations.literal: Initially, Nao Chi killed Min Wang, Ju people sought Min Wang son Fa Zhang, got him Grand Historian Tao home, for person irrigated garden.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Nao Chi killed King Min, the people of Ju searched for the king's son Fa Zhang. They found him in the household of the Grand Historian Jiao, where he had been working as a gardener.

sentences.zh: 嬓女憐而善遇之。

translations.literal: Tao daughter pitied good treated him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's daughter took pity on him and treated him with kindness.

sentences.zh: 後法章私以情告女，女遂與通。

translations.literal: Later Fa Zhang secretly with feelings told girl, girl then with him had relations.
translations.idiomatic: In time, Fa Zhang secretly revealed his true identity to the girl, and she became his lover.

sentences.zh: 及莒人共立法章為齊王，以莒距燕，而太史氏女遂為后，所謂「君王后」也。

translations.literal: When the people of Ju together established Fa Zhang as King of Qi and used Ju to resist Yan, the Grand Historian's daughter then became queen — the one called 'Junwang Hou'.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Ju jointly established Fa Zhang as King of Qi and used Ju as their stronghold against Yan, the daughter of the Grand Historian clan became his queen — the one known as "Queen Junwang."

sentences.zh: 燕之初入齊，聞畫邑人王蠋賢，令軍中曰「環畫邑三十里無入」，以王蠋之故。

translations.literal: Yan initially entered Qi, heard Hua yi person Wang Juan worthy, ordered army middle said 'surround Hua yi thirty li none enter', because Wang Juan reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first entered Qi, they heard that a man named Wang Zhu of the town of Huayi was a worthy. The general ordered his army: "No one shall enter within thirty li of Huayi." This was done out of respect for Wang Zhu.

sentences.zh: 已而使人謂蠋曰：「齊人多高子之義，吾以子為將，封子萬家。」

translations.literal: Soon after sent person told Juan said: 'Qi people much esteem your righteousness, I make you general, enfeoff you ten thousand households.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, he sent a messenger to say to Wang Zhu: "Many of the people of Qi esteem your sense of righteousness. I wish to appoint you my general and enfeoff you with ten thousand households."

sentences.zh: 蠋固謝。

translations.literal: Juan firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 燕人曰：「子不聽，吾引三軍而屠畫邑。」

translations.literal: Yan person said: 'You not listen, I lead three armies slaughter Hua yi.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yan commander replied, "If you will not comply, I shall lead my armies to slaughter the people of Huayi."

sentences.zh: 王蠋曰：「忠臣不事二君，貞女不更二夫。

translations.literal: Wang Juan said: 'Loyal minister not serve two lords, chaste woman not change two husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu answered, "A loyal minister does not serve two lords, just as a virtuous woman does not take a second husband.

sentences.zh: 齊王不聽吾諫，故退而耕於野。

translations.literal: Qi king not listen my advice, thus retreated farmed in wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qi would not heed my counsel, so I withdrew and tilled the fields.

sentences.zh: 國既破亡，吾不能存；

translations.literal: State already broken perished, I cannot preserve;
translations.idiomatic: Now the state is destroyed, and I could not preserve it;

sentences.zh: 今又劫之以兵為君將，是助桀為暴也。

translations.literal: Now again coerce with troops make me your general, this help Jie do tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would coerce me with armed force to serve as your general — that would be to aid a tyrant in his violence.

sentences.zh: 與其生而無義，固不如烹！」

translations.literal: Rather than live without righteousness, certainly better to be cooked!'
translations.idiomatic: Rather than live without righteousness, I would sooner be boiled alive!"

sentences.zh: 遂經其頸於樹枝，自奮絕脰而死。

translations.literal: Then hung his neck on tree branch, self exerted broke neck died.
translations.idiomatic: He then tied his neck to a tree branch, strained with all his might until his neck snapped, and died.

sentences.zh: 齊亡大夫聞之，曰：「王蠋，布衣也，義不北面於燕，況在位食祿者乎！」

translations.literal: Qi perished grandees heard this, said: 'Wang Juan, commoner, righteousness not face north to Yan, moreover officials in position eating salary!'
translations.idiomatic: When the exiled officials of Qi heard of this, they said, "Wang Zhu was a mere commoner, yet his sense of righteousness would not allow him to face north and submit to Yan. How much more should this be true of those of us who held office and drew a salary!"

sentences.zh: 乃相聚如莒，求諸子，立為襄王。

translations.literal: Then mutually gathered like Ju, sought various sons, established as Xiang Wang.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered together and went to Ju, where they sought out the royal heirs and established one of them as King Xiang.
